first.rationale: Three simultaneous pressures compete for the single experiment slot: competitor pricing, falling activation, falling onboarding completion. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting reactive move given competitor entry pricing, but the objective is 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue,' and matching a price war risks attracting low-quality, margin-eroding accounts rather than qualified revenue — I want to verify the original record to see if it actually measured retention/quality or just short-term acquisition lift before trusting it under this new competitive context. I'm flagging that risk rather than acting on it this week. Onboarding completion decline (4%) has two corroborating inherited memories (memory_31 signup simplification, memory_86 shortened onboarding) pointing to a well-tested, lower-risk lever with durable prior success in the exact segment under pressure (self-serve/SMB), which is also the segment the competitor is targeting — improving onboarding strengthens defensibility without a margin-cutting price response. I verify memory_31 to confirm the original signup-simplification result still generalizes to current SMB conditions before committing the week's only experiment slot to it, and verify memory_73 to check whether promotional pricing's 'sustainable' framing holds up or was only short-horizon. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a reasonable alternative but activation decline may be partly downstream of the onboarding drop, so fixing onboarding first is the more root-cause-oriented, reversible bet.
